mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% annualized over the past two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL increases are not followed by tighter monetary policy within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in the past month signals a tightening labor market, which leads to increased wage pressures and subsequently higher inflation expectations, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE decreases are not followed by increased inflation expectations within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past three months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansionary demand periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the past two months signals increased economic activity and supply-side strength, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increases are not followed by increased economic activity within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, the combination signals a restrictive monetary policy in a tight labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy with tight labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the specified conditions are not followed by a contraction in economic activity within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in the past two months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST decreases are not followed by a broader economic slowdown within the next year.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in the past month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains below 5%, it signals a strong labor market with low unemployment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: strong labor market with low unemployment
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the specified conditions are not followed by increased consumer spending within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over the past quarter signals a strong economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in mid-cycle expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
